Subject: v4 rollout - sudden p99 and 5xx spike (URGENT)

Jordan —

We rolled v4 (model v4.0 + new int8 quant profile) to production at 02:00 PT this morning and immediately saw a sharp jump in p99 latency (from ~420ms to >1.9s) and backend 500 errors climb to ~3.6% of requests. Throughput throttled shortly after. This is our peak window and it is directly impacting live transactions. Attached is a short perf capture and request sample (fairway_v4_perf_report.pdf).

Key symptoms:
- p50 roughly stable, p95 up ~2x, p99 up ~4x
- error pattern: 500s concentrated on long-context requests (>1024 tokens)
- throughput fall: sustained ~25% drop in qps vs previous baseline
- observable drop in answer coherence for multi-turn flows (customers noticing hallucinations)

We need immediate remediation: either rollback to v3 or an emergency patch. Please advise what you can do now and whether you can commit to a rollback window to restore SLA.

Aisha Kumar
Head of Platform Reliability
FairwayTech

Quick ops snapshot: attaching ops_snapshot.json. Observations from infra:
- No GPU OOMs or host-level OOMs. Utilization modestly higher (~70% -> ~82%) but not saturated.
- Significant increase in tail RPC latencies between frontend proxies and model workers (connection churn noted).
- Worker logs show intermittent "KV_CACHE_MISS_SEVERE" and longer decode stalls (microsecond to millisecond spikes accumulating).
- Autoscaler triggered additional workers, but they warmed slowly due to model download + quant table compile time (~45s).

Initial hypothesis: quant profile for int8 is changing execution path (kernel selection) which increases per-token execution time on long-context requests and causes cache behaviour regressions. Also seeing elevated retry counts from frontend which magnify p99.

Next: will try to pin traffic to fallback model variant and capture traces for a 15-min window.

Ben — thanks for the snapshot. We dug into the traces from the warmed workers and found: 

Root cause (preliminary):
- The new int8 quant profile changed the compute path for attention kernels on sequences >1024. At compile time the runtime chose a different fused kernel optimized for shorter sequences; that kernel degenerates for long contexts and causes excessive memory thrash and KV cache fragmentation.
- This led to elevated decode stalls on the hot path and increased tail latency. The increased retry behavior at the gateway amplified the visible p99.
- Coherence drop appears to be related to subtle rounding differences introduced by the quant tables for multi-turn prefix caching — some prompt prefixes diverge leading to different attention weight dynamics for later turns.

Immediate mitigations we can execute in ~30–45 minutes:
1) Route FairwayTech traffic to the vetted v4-fallback variant (same weights, old quant table) — quick switch in routing table (no model download).
2) If routing not sufficient, schedule a rollback to v3.9 for the account (needs infra change + warm-up) — target 60-minute window.
3) Disable the new int8 kernel selection flag and force the longer-seq optimized kernel in runtime; this requires a short hotfix deploy to model workers but minimal risk.

I will prepare a small patch with the kernel selection override and the rollback diff; attaching rollback-diff.patch. Recommend we attempt routing to fallback first, then kernel-override, then rollback if needed.

Irene Choi
Director, Serving Runtime Engineering, Redwood Inference

1) Immediate: route your traffic to the v4-fallback variant (no model file change) — this will be applied now and should reduce p99 within minutes if kernel selection is the issue. We will monitor for 30 minutes.
2) Near-term (30–90 min): if p99 remains high, we will apply a runtime override to force the long-seq optimized kernel (hotfix deploy, minimal worker restart).
3) Contingency (if the two steps fail): schedule rollback to v3.9 with a 60-minute window. We will prepare a rollback runbook and warm workers in advance to reduce cutover time.

Requested approval for step 1 now and for the contingency rollback window (proposed 13:00–14:00 PT) if needed. Also, please confirm whether you want us to hold traffic to a single region during the change.
